video.title: Would You Take a Flier On a Starting Center at Pick 120?

summary: Josh Lloyd goes through about 50 late-round flier targets for fantasy basketball drafts. The main 15 have an ADP or rank of 115 or worse in at least three of five sources (Yahoo rank, Yahoo ADP, ESPN rank, ESPN ADP, Fantrax ADP). For the rapid-fire list, a player only needs to be outside 115 in one of them. His top targets include Jusuf Nurkic, Keegan Murray, Collin Murray-Boyles, Jeremiah Fears, Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg, Jalen Green, Ajay Mitchell, Cam Johnson, Egor Demin, Gui Santos, Khaman Maluach, Isaiah Jackson, Daniel Gafford and Yves Missi. His main point is that from round 10 on, you should swing for upside on players who might start or have a wide range of outcomes, instead of taking safe players whose value you can find on waivers. He also says it is fine to take losses in weeks one and two while you wait for fliers to pan out.

rules.text: Once your starting slots are filled, use bench picks on upside fliers. Round 10 can already be a flier zone.
rules.quote: I'm talking about at least all of your bench slots. Once you start filling once you've filled up all your starters

rules.text: Do not draft a player at pick 110 who projects to finish 110th. You can find that kind of value on the waiver wire.
rules.quote: there's no point grabbing a guy at 110 who's going to be 110th. There's no point in that.

rules.text: Take upside players in round 10 instead of waiting for their ADP. You usually drop and stream your round 10 to 13 picks anyway.
rules.quote: for most of your teams, you're going to drop your round 10, 11, 12, 13 players nearly all the time.

rules.text: Projections are a median outcome. When two players have the same projection, prefer the one with the wider range of outcomes. Veterans like Harrison Barnes or Tobias Harris have no realistic path above their projection.
rules.quote: But the band of what he can do is a lot wider than what others can do.

rules.text: Take a flier on a player only if there is a real chance he starts or gets a role. If reports say he will not start, pass.
rules.quote: So if he might start, I will take the chance on. If we know that he won't, then I won't take it.

rules.text: Value players against consensus, not on personal bias. Draft a player you don't like when his price and your team's needs make sense.
rules.quote: It's more about how do I value them versus consensus? How do I value their game versus how other people do?

rules.text: Don't draft for the week one schedule or stream just to get extra games early. Accept losses in weeks one and two to hold fliers with longer-term value.
rules.quote: I'm okay to do that and take L's in week one because if I draft Gillespie or use him

rules.text: Injury-prone stashes like Kristaps Porzingis are hard to use in daily-change leagues with small benches. Fit the pick to your format.
rules.quote: If you're in a daily changes league with small benches, it's almost impossible to deal with that.

rules.text: Ignore what players say about each other. Players are poor evaluators of talent.
rules.quote: I do not care. players who are the worst evaluators of talent. What they say, not in a million years.

rules.text: Avoid single-season myopia. One bad season does not make a player bad.
rules.quote: Miles was pretty bad last season, but people again single season myopia.

rules.text: Backups who are one injury away from starting are valid late fliers.
rules.quote: if one of Green, Booker, and Brooks gets hurt, Gillespie will start. He'll play 30 minutes and he'll be worth it.
